title: RT by @covenant_ai: Templar's work reduces to one question. How much of the machine-learning lifecycle can run across ordinary networks instead of a single datacentre? Pre-training answered first, with Covenant-72B as the proof at scale. Post-training followed through our communication-efficiency research. Serving open models on distributed hardware is the piece we are working on now, and it is the one that puts the whole arc in front of users. The internet is the datacentre.

name: Covenant AI
title: RT by @covenant_ai: PULSE (also called Delta weight sync) has become one of the most important ideas in RL infrastructure this year. Our paper, posted on February 3, explained why it loses nothing. At RL learning rates, about 99% of each step's weight updates disappear in the BF16 cast, so the inference workers never see them. Since then, @huggingface has built Delta Weight Sync for TRL and vLLM on that argument. @FireworksAI_HQ cites PULSE, and its ARCv3 compressor now makes the updates even smaller. This week @humansand reported pausing inference for only about 220 milliseconds per update on Blackwell GPUs. PULSE has now been accepted at AXIOM, a @NeurIPSConf 2026 workshop. https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03839

title: RT by @covenant_ai: Crucible, Templar's pre-training platform, has completed its first production end-to-end training runs. The latest trained an 8B model on 50.53B tokens across 48 distributed A100s, at an estimated $0.1202 per million tokens of GPU rental. The run reached 48.3% effective MFU. At AWS p4de Capacity Blocks pricing, a 48-A100 cluster operating at the literature-derived 65% compute ceiling comes to an estimated $0.1686 per million tokens. Crucible's measured $0.1202 was about 29% lower after its low-bandwidth overhead. The comparison excludes R2 storage and operations. The full writeup shows the method and accounting. Blog: https://www.tplr.ai/publications/blog/introducing-crucible
